newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian stocks end down as C-C Amatil slips on downgrade.
newsitem.headline: Australian stocks end down as C-C Amatil slips on downgrade.

text.p: Australian shares closed slightly weaker on Monday with opening gains eradicated by afternoon profit-taking after the market was held back by a sell-off of Coca-Cola Amatil stock.
Key share market barometer, the All Ordinaries index, closed 3.5 points lower at 2,383.8, after hitting an intra-day and all-time high of 2,398.6 during early morning trade.
Trading was active as engineering group ANI topped turnover after major shareholder Ross Palmer sold 40 million shares.

"The market was doing alright even with the slump in Coca-Coal Amatil stock this morning but this afternoon investors took the top off the market across the board," said Eric Gale, director of institutions at Sydney brokerage, Ord Minnett.
Gale said the late sell-down could be attributed to profit-taking after the market's strong rise in the past two session in the past week.
"The market expected Coca-Cola to get slammed, and that's exactly what happened," Gale said.
Coca-Cola Amatil disappointed investors late on Friday when it warned that its 1996 profit would be flat. The company's shares closed A$2.04 (US$1.61) weaker at A$15.50 (US$12.25).
Dealers said that because the market had the weekend to digest Coca-Cola Amatil's profit downgrade, it was possible the company's shares could make a slight recovery within the next two sessions.

Major banks were the most noticeable targets of profit-taking with the National Australia Bank and Commonwealth Bank losing all their early gains, while resource majors BHP and CRA ended firmer but off the day's highs.
Behind the strength of the resources sector was the more robust outlook for base metal prices, after copper found good support in active trade on the London Metal Exchange on Friday.
